title: Quiz: What Is Data Mining? The Big Data Landscape and the KDD Process

questions.text: Which of the six mining tasks is used to group policyholders into behavioural segments WITHOUT using pre-defined labels?
questions.explanation: Clustering is unsupervised — it discovers natural groupings in data without relying on labelled categories. Classification, by contrast, requires pre-defined labels (e.g. churned vs. not churned).

questions.text: Which of the 4 Vs of Big Data refers to the trustworthiness and accuracy of the data?
questions.explanation: Veracity concerns data quality — whether the data can be trusted. Volume is about size, Velocity about arrival speed, and Variety about different data types.

questions.text: In the KDD process, which step comes immediately BEFORE the data mining step?
questions.explanation: The KDD steps are: Selection → Preprocessing → Transformation → Data Mining → Interpretation. Transformation (feature engineering, scaling, encoding) is the step immediately before applying a mining algorithm.

questions.text: You want to predict whether a health insurance claim is fraudulent (yes/no). Which mining task is most appropriate?
options: Regression, because you are predicting a score
Classification, because the outcome is a discrete label
Clustering, because fraud is an anomaly
Association rule mining, because fraud involves co-occurring events
questions.explanation: Fraud detection with a yes/no outcome is a binary classification problem. The model learns to map input features to one of two classes. Anomaly detection is an alternative approach, but the question specifies predicting a labelled outcome (fraudulent vs. not), which is classification.

questions.text: The KDD process is strictly linear: once you move from preprocessing to transformation, you never return to earlier steps.
questions.explanation: KDD is iterative, not linear. After mining, you may discover that a key variable has systematic errors that require returning to the preprocessing step. Real projects cycle through the steps multiple times.

questions.text: skimr::skim() is most useful for which stage of the KDD process?
options: Data Mining — it implements the mining algorithm
Selection — it identifies which data sources to use
Preprocessing — it reveals missing values, skewness, and outliers
Interpretation — it explains why patterns exist
questions.explanation: skim() provides summary statistics (mean, sd, percentiles, completion rate) that help you diagnose data quality issues — exactly what you need during the preprocessing stage. It does not perform mining or explain causes.
